clue.text: Oban chasm wrecked this vehicle

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed apart, so the letters before it are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: the place name and the gorge taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A carriage comes to grief in a ravine near the Scottish port of Oban.
explanation.walkthrough: Oban is a harbour town in western Scotland; 'this vehicle' points back at the wrecked letters, which form the very thing that was wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom cab is a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Very big embrace needs energy

blocks.note: to embrace someone is to hug them
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A really big hug takes some effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge is a straightforward synonym for enormous or very big.

clue.text: Up or down, it's the same time

indicators.text: Up or down, it's the same
indicators.note: in a down entry, reading upwards or downwards giving the same word describes a word that reads identically both ways

blocks.note: a particular time of day which also reads the same backwards

explanation.surface: A riddle about a clock reading that looks the same whichever way up it is held.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue except the last word describes the entry's shape: a four-letter time that is spelt identically top to bottom and bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is midday, twelve o'clock, a specific time of day.

clue.text: Mail going off in distant settlement?

blocks.note: a light going off is out
letters and parcels are post

explanation.surface: Letters being sent off to a remote colony.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse of clue order: the word for 'going off' leads, followed by the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small remote settlement or station far from the main centre.

clue.text: Caught by old mine, get punished

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
O is a standard abbreviation for old
a coal mine is a pit

explanation.surface: A miner caught down an old mine gets into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Cop it is informal British English for being punished or getting into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop it is a colloquial idiom meaning to be in trouble or receive punishment.

clue.text: Boatman's song in pub, with girl

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A sailor sings in the pub alongside a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a Venetian gondolier's song, so literally the song of a boatman.

clue.text: Penny-pinch to cream off pounds at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: to skim is to take the cream off milk
the initial of this word

explanation.surface: A miser economising by creaming off cash at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to be stingy, spending too little, which is what a penny-pincher does.

clue.text: American turns up drinking round, with call for getting bitter

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top
drinking takes something inside, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: US is short for American
O is round in shape
to call someone on the phone is to ring them

explanation.surface: An American shows up in a bar, buys a round and phones someone, growing sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Souring means turning sour, becoming bitter or resentful.

clue.text: Those who start riots? I ain't involved!

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters as printed, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: Someone protesting innocence when asked who stirred up the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those who start riots' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'start'; the riots are part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Initiators are people who begin or set something in motion.

clue.text: Promotional function, one covering avoidance

blocks.note: PR, public relations, is promotional work
a social function is an event
the Roman numeral one
something on top of another is covering it

explanation.surface: A publicity event where someone is busy hiding from attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Prevention is the act of stopping something happening, so a means of avoidance.

clue.text: Spirit provided by good innkeeper

blocks.note: G is short for good
an innkeeper hosts guests

explanation.surface: A landlord serves up a drink of spirits in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' tempts as alcohol from the innkeeper; it is the supernatural kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is a spirit of the dead, a phantom.

clue.text: Animal getting gold trophy in softwood case

indicators.note: being in a case means sitting inside its walls

blocks.note: pine is a softwood, here acting as the outer case
or is the heraldic word for gold
a cup is a trophy

explanation.surface: A prize animal is given a gold cup displayed in a wooden cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: The porcupine is a spiny rodent, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Unfortunately sire, I can't row the other way round

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go wrong, so these letters end up out of their order

blocks.note: the letters as printed, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: A servant apologises to his lord for being unable to row the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrariwise means conversely, in the opposite direction or manner.

clue.text: Book studied on deal? This may help when using one's loaf!

definitions.text: This may help when using one's loaf

blocks.note: B is short for book
to read a subject is to study it
deal is pine or fir timber, sawn into a board

explanation.surface: Reading up before a business deal is a case of using your head.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' means placed above. 'Using one's loaf' is British slang for thinking, but here the loaf is bread being sliced.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadboard is the wooden board a loaf is cut on, so it helps when slicing bread.

clue.text: River good and straight?

blocks.note: the Forth is a river in Scotland
right means good or proper

explanation.surface: Asking whether a river is pleasant and runs in a straight line.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthright means direct and frank, speaking straight without evasion.

clue.text: Cocky individual invading kangaroo's territory

indicators.note: the answer invades the following words, lying across their boundary

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: An arrogant person trespassing on an Australian marsupial's land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocky' looks like it means arrogant, but it points to a cock, a male bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a cock, a male chicken, so playfully a cocky individual.

clue.text: Salesman acting as consumer, doing it again

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
someone eating is consuming food

explanation.surface: A salesman playing the customer, going through the motions once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating means performing the same action once more.

clue.text: Although only half, explosive should not …

indicators.note: keeping only half a word means the other half is cut away

blocks.note: taken as written; just its back four letters survive
TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene

explanation.surface: A warning that explosive should not be used, even in small amounts.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the sentence on into the next clue; it adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oughtn't is the contraction of ought not, meaning should not.

clue.text: … in this measure, blow the lid off Hades!

indicators.note: removing a lid takes off the top, the first letter of the word

blocks.note: Hades is the underworld, hell

explanation.surface: Continuing the warning: explosives in these quantities would blow hell open.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues from the previous one; an ell is an old cloth measure of about 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old unit of length used for measuring cloth.

clue.text: A new idiot in an old city

blocks.note: taken as written
N is short for new
a twerp is a silly person

explanation.surface: A newly arrived fool wandering about an ancient town.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a Belgian port with a medieval centre, an old city.

clue.text: Once healthy son pants?

blocks.note: ex means former, once
hale means healthy
S is short for son

explanation.surface: A query whether trousers once belonged to a healthy son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a noun for trousers or, in Britain, underwear, but it is a verb: breathes hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pants breathes out heavily, so the verb forms match: exhales.

clue.text: Rob upset with game ban

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Rob is upset at being barred from playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' reads as a verb or a name; it is just three letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade, so a ban.

clue.text: Initially, botulism threat with alien meat joint

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the initial of this word
a threat is a risk
ET, the film extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A cut of meat carrying the danger of food poisoning from outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a cut of beef from the breast, a joint of meat.

clue.text: What one wears when there's nothing on?

definitions.text: What one wears when there's nothing on?

blocks.clueFragment: What one wears when there's nothing on?
blocks.note: surface reading: casual clothes for a day with no engagements
setter's reading: wearing no clothes at all, i.e. naked as at birth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing on' suggests an empty diary, but it means no clothes; the 'outfit' is one's bare skin, the one worn at birth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular idiom for nakedness, the skin a person was born in.

clue.text: Almost say hello meeting bishop, respected person in India

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
hi is a greeting
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Greeting a bishop politely, as one would an esteemed person in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib is a respectful form of address used in colonial India for a man of status.

clue.text: Regret after end of fight? Correct

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word that follows
after means the first piece comes later in the answer than the second

blocks.note: the closing letter of this word
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Feeling remorse once a fight is over, and rightly so.
explanation.definitionFit: True can mean accurate or correct, as in a true statement.

clue.text: Hock piece of little value

blocks.note: first meaning: to pledge an item for a loan
second meaning: the lowest-ranked chess piece

explanation.walkthrough: Hock is also a German white wine, which a solver might chase first; here it is the verb meaning to leave something at a moneylender's.
explanation.definitionFit: To pawn is to deposit goods as security; the pawn is the weakest chessman.

clue.text: Half singe cooked sea creature

indicators.note: cooking changes ingredients into something new, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A seafood dish only partly charred in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' looks like an instruction to keep part of 'singe', but every letter of both words goes into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The angelfish is a brightly coloured fish of reefs and warm seas, a sea creature.

clue.text: Fate may be more peaceful, as some say

indicators.note: points to how the word sounds in some speakers' mouths, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: calmer, said in a non-rhotic accent with no final R

explanation.surface: Destiny might turn out more serene, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: The match works only in accents that drop the R, as in southern British English.
explanation.definitionFit: Karma, in Hindu and Buddhist thought, is the moral law of cause and effect, loosely one's destiny.

clue.text: Is fond of taking part in commando tests

indicators.note: the answer takes part in the following words, being a portion of them

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Someone who enjoys joining in military fitness trials.
explanation.definitionFit: To dote on someone is to be excessively fond of them.

clue.text: Begone wet, frightful middleman!

indicators.note: something frightful is a dreadful mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone shooing away a feeble intermediary, wet being British slang for a weakling.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between is an intermediary who carries messages between parties.
